description: Structured eval definitions for the EFS Access Points Deployer. Five-case proven set exercising READY_TO_DEPLOY / PREREQUISITES_MISSING across access-point creation with POSIX identity, mount-target gaps, IAM enforcement with the AccessPointArn Deny, EKS CSI driver integration, and Lambda cross-AZ mount-target gaps. Each eval maps to a prompt file and a baseline (no-skill) file for with-skill-vs-baseline comparison.

eval_cases.name: EFS access point with POSIX identity, root directory, TLS
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — AP with PosixUser + RootDirectory + CreationInfo + TLS mount
eval_cases.prompt: Create an EFS access point for file system fs-0abc123def (account 123456789012, region us-east-1). AP name: team-a-ap. Root directory path: /data/team-a with auto-creation (owner uid 1000, gid 1000, permissions 0750). POSIX user identity: uid 1000, gid 1000, secondary gids 2000. The file system has encryption at rest, bursting throughput, mount targets in use1-az1, use1-az2, use1-az3, and Intelligent-Tiering lifecycle (IA after 30 days). amazon-efs-utils is installed on the EC2 ASG. Include TLS encryption in transit.
eval_cases.expected_output:
ACCESS_POINT: team-a-ap
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] File-system baseline: fs-0abc123def, Encrypted=true, ThroughputMode=bursting
  [✓] Mount targets in every compute AZ: 3 AZs covered (use1-az1, use1-az2, use1-az3)
  [✓] amazon-efs-utils installed on EC2 ASG
  [✓] Access point created: team-a-ap (root: /data/team-a, uid: 1000, gid: 1000, perms: 0750)
  [✓] File-system policy: Deny on Null:AccessPointArn + Allow through AP
  [✓] Mount via AP alias with TLS: mount -t efs -o tls,accesspoint=<AP_ID>
  [OPTIONAL] (ECS/EKS) Integration: not requested
  [OPTIONAL] (Lambda) Function VPC + AP: not requested
  [✓] Intelligent-Tiering lifecycle: TransitionTo IA after 30 days
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws efs describe-access-points --file-system-id fs-0abc123def
  aws efs describe-file-system-policy --file-system-id fs-0abc123def
  aws efs describe-mount-targets --file-system-id fs-0abc123def
  aws efs describe-lifecycle-configuration --file-system-id fs-0abc123def

eval_cases.name: Three compute AZs but only two mount targets — must flag gap
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — mount target absent in us-west-2c
eval_cases.prompt: Create an EFS access point "internal-logs-ap" for file system fs-998877 in account 123456789012 region us-west-2. Compute runs in us-west-2a, us-west-2b, and us-west-2c, but I just checked and mount targets exist only in 2a and 2b. File system has encryption at rest. POSIX uid 1001, gid 1001, root path /logs. Add the IAM file-system policy that forces access-point-only mounts.
eval_cases.expected_output:
ACCESS_POINT: internal-logs-ap
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] File-system baseline: fs-998877, Encrypted=true
  [✗] Mount targets in every compute AZ: us-west-2c has no mount target — create one in subnet-2c before proceeding
  [✓] amazon-efs-utils: cannot verify until target host is selected
  [✓] Access point created: internal-logs-ap (root: /logs, uid: 1001, gid: 1001)
  [✗] File-system policy: blocked pending mount target gap
  [✗] Mount via AP alias with TLS: blocked pending mount target
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws efs describe-mount-targets --file-system-id fs-998877
  aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=us-west-2c

eval_cases.name: IAM file-system policy with the Null:AccessPointArn Deny closing the DNS-name bypass
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — Allow with AP ARN condition + Deny on Null:AccessPointArn
eval_cases.prompt: Create an EFS access point "prod-app-ap" on fs-aaaabbbbcccc (account 123456789012, region us-east-1). POSIX identity uid 2000, gid 2000, root /app, perms 0750. Attach a file-system policy that enforces access-point-only mounts: allow ClientMount + ClientWrite + ClientRootAccess through the AP ARN condition, AND deny any mount that did NOT come through an access point. All three AZs have mount targets; amazon-efs-utils is installed on the EC2 hosts.
eval_cases.expected_output:
ACCESS_POINT: prod-app-ap
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] File-system baseline: fs-aaaabbbbcccc
  [✓] Mount targets in every compute AZ: 3 AZs covered
  [✓] amazon-efs-utils installed
  [✓] Access point created: prod-app-ap (root: /app, uid: 2000, gid: 2000, perms: 0750)
  [✓] File-system policy: Allow with elasticfilesystem:AccessPointArn + Deny on Null:AccessPointArn
  [✓] Mount via AP alias with TLS: mount -t efs -o tls,accesspoint=<AP_ID>
  [OPTIONAL] (ECS/EKS) Integration: not requested
  [OPTIONAL] (Lambda) Function VPC + AP: not requested
  [✓] Intelligent-Tiering lifecycle: verify present
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws efs describe-access-points --file-system-id fs-aaaabbbbcccc
  aws efs describe-file-system-policy --file-system-id fs-aaaabbbbcccc

eval_cases.name: EKS EFS CSI driver with dynamic access-point provisioning and ClientRootAccess
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — CSI driver StorageClass with provisioningMode efs-ap + IRSA role including ClientRootAccess
eval_cases.prompt: Set up EKS cluster "prod-cluster" to consume an existing EFS file system fs-ccccdddddddd (account 123456789012, region us-east-1) via the EFS CSI driver. I want dynamic access-point provisioning per PVC with directoryPerms 700 and gidRange 1000-2000. The CSI driver IRSA role is arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/efs-csi-driver-role. Verify the IRSA role includes ClientRootAccess. Mount targets exist in all three AZs.
eval_cases.expected_output:
ACCESS_POINT: efs-csi-dynamic
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] File-system baseline: fs-ccccdddddddd
  [✓] Mount targets in every compute AZ: 3 AZs covered
  [✓] EFS CSI driver installed on EKS prod-cluster
  [✓] Access point mode: dynamic per PVC via provisioningMode efs-ap
  [✓] File-system policy: verify IAM allows the IRSA role
  [✓] Mount via CSI driver with access points
  [✓] (ECS/EKS) Integration wired: EKS StorageClass efs-sc, directoryPerms 700, gidRange 1000-2000
  [OPTIONAL] (Lambda) Function VPC + AP: not requested
  [✓] IRSA role includes elasticfilesystem:ClientRootAccess
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app=efs-csi-controller
  kubectl get storageclass efs-sc
  aws iam get-role-policy --role-name efs-csi-driver-role

eval_cases.name: Lambda EFS mount with subnets in two AZs but mount target in only one
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — Lambda subnet in use1-az2 has no corresponding mount target
eval_cases.prompt: Configure Lambda function "file-processor" to mount EFS file system fs-eeeeffff0000 (account 123456789012, region us-east-1) via access point fsap-9999aaaa2222 at /mnt/efs. The function's VPC config has subnets in use1-az1 (subnet-aaa) and use1-az2 (subnet-bbb). I just checked and the EFS has a mount target only in use1-az1. The function execution role has ClientMount + ClientWrite + ClientRootAccess. Make sure the mount works in both AZs.
eval_cases.expected_output:
ACCESS_POINT: fsap-9999aaaa2222
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] File-system baseline: fs-eeeeffff0000
  [✗] Mount targets in every compute AZ: use1-az2 has no mount target — Lambda cold starts in subnet-bbb will time out at 50s
  [✓] Access point exists: fsap-9999aaaa2222
  [✓] Lambda role includes ClientMount + ClientWrite + ClientRootAccess
  [✗] (Lambda) Function VPC + AP: blocked pending mount target in use1-az2
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws efs describe-mount-targets --file-system-id fs-eeeeffff0000
  aws ec2 describe-subnets --subnet-ids subnet-bbb --query 'Subnets[0].AvailabilityZone'
